title: Keyline tone anchors and edge rhythm token revision
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Replace ad-hoc color/spacing variants with a keyline-driven token set that ties tone anchors to component keylines and an edge-rhythm spacing/radius system. This effort reduces token permutations, improves legibility at small sizes, and makes elevation steps predictable for charts and data surfaces.

Scope: color palette rebaseline (surface/interactive/neutral/attention ramps), a compact but expressive typography delta for dense tables, an edge rhythm (spacing & radius) mapped to keyline multiples instead of absolute pixels, and a micro-elevation stack for small layered surfaces (tooltips, popovers, table-rows). Applies to core primitives (button, table row, card, chart layers, form fields).

Why now: Recent regressions in readability at 12px table rows plus inconsistent corner radii across controls have produced visual noise in dense analytics pages. Unifying on keyline multiples and anchored tones will reduce cognitive load for designers and eliminate many component-level overrides.

Key decisions proposed: 1) Introduce 5 tone anchors per semantic family (surface-0..4) where surface-0 is background and surface-4 is strong interactive surface. Keep hue similar to current palette but rebalance lightness for contrast targets. 2) Edge rhythm defined as [4,8,12,16,24]px multiples for spacing and correlated radius tokens (radii = spacing * 0.75 for small, 1.0 for medium, 1.5 for large). 3) Micro-elevation stack with 3 discrete levels (none / soft / raised) implemented as combined shadow + alpha overlay to ensure consistent color blending on charts and tables. 4) Typography scale: add a condensed micro-headline and a refined 11px data-caption with adjusted letterspacing for table density.

Migration notes: Provide a token-mapping script that converts legacy tokens (e.g., token.background.surfaceA -> surface-0) and a lint rule to flag direct hex usage in components. Storybook token-preview story will be updated before rollout. Engineering will receive a JSON token bundle and a CSS variables shim for older apps.

Dependencies: Requires a brief runtime feature-flag for token swap and a release window with QA on analytics pages. Accessibility review to verify AA contrast for primary interactive colors and AAA for labels where possible.

2025-02-18 - Rafael: sketched token mapping and prepared Figma token file; shared figma link in design_links. Need engineering input on shadow implementation (composite alpha vs. separate layers).
2025-02-21 - Miguel Ortega (Eng): reviewed approach; asked for concrete token->css var mapping and an automated migration plan for legacy CSS modules.
2025-02-25 - Accessibility review (Elena Novak): initial palette fails 14px button label contrast on dark theme; adjusted anchor pairings recommended.
2025-03-02 - Rafael: updated micro-elevation specs to use overlay alpha 6% + subtle y-offset to avoid aliasing on charts. Attached draft PR for storybook previews.

acceptance_criteria: All core components consume new tokens via CSS variables and components refactorables are merged in feature branch.
Token migration script converts legacy tokens in the codebase with <=2% manual edits required and produces a migration report.
Contrast targets: interactive labels meet WCAG AA on both light and dark themes across recommended sizes.
Storybook includes a token gallery showing tone anchors, spacing grid overlay, and micro-elevation samples for buttons, tables, and charts.
Rollout documented: feature flag path, QA checklist, and rollback steps included in rollout_plan.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge token bundle behind feature flag. 2) Run automated migration script on staging, review migration report, fix any manual mappings. 3) Enable tokens for internal beta route (console beta) for 48 hours; collect visual diffs on dashboard and reports. 4) Run accessibility smoke tests and manual QA on dense analytics pages. 5) Gradual rollout across accounts over 7 days with monitoring for layout regressions. Rollback by toggling feature flag and reapplying legacy CSS shim.
